Hi Alex —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is a short packet for procurement titled "For Procurement: econ assumptions (MAP)". Quick executive summary for your team to paste into the packet:

- Baseline assumptions (conservative): 350 tokens/call; 125k tokens per $1 (hosted, quantized config).
- Sensitivity: cache hit at 10% increases monthly spend by ~35% vs baseline; at 50% it reduces spend by ~12%.
- Batching benefit: avg batch size 1 (no batching) = baseline; size 4 ≈ 18% tokens/$ improvement; size 8 ≈ 27% improvement. These gains assume Redwood continuous batching and the same model family.
- Latency: batching improves cost but can add tail latency under small-burst traffic — see batching_latency_sample.csv for numbers. Prefetch/KV cache reduces tokens/call by avoiding repeated prompt context for returning users (see prefetch-impact-summary.pdf).

Action items / next steps we recommend in MAP:
1) Pilot measurement: instrument token counts and cache hit rate during the first 2 weeks of pilot (we'll provide a small telemetry dashboard).
2) If measured cache hit < 20% at pilot, plan a prefetched-KV optimization sprint (3 weeks) to raise hits toward 30–40% and reduce spend.
3) Agree on a 30-day lookback for traffic used in the MAP to re-evaluate tokens/$ and batching configs before move to Dedicated.

If procurement needs the packet as a PDF (single file) or a one-line econ summary for execs, tell me which format and I'll send it.

Best,
